verdict: fail (6.8 < 7.5). The draft is unusually honest and internally consistent: I spot-checked the headline numbers (D, matched-slip D 0.4563 by interpolating the Fig. 1b points, hold-force difference 1.085 N, break-even times 16.56 / 32.99 / 28.61 s, integrated force-time) and they agree across abstract, tables, figure prompt and text. Claims are scoped to simulation, to the marginal per-stratum in-expectation bound, and to the design. The problem is substance. The one confirmed pre-registered result holds on a design the paper itself calls weak by construction (friction independent of every non-tactile input). It shrinks to D 0.14 at sigma 0.4 and reverses for mu in [0.5, 0.8]. The pre-registered learned arm shows no gain over a plug-in. The attribution claim ('the saving is in the probe') rests on post hoc, unadjusted, slip-unmatched rows on a refined grid that was adopted after the primary grid floored the plug-in. The break-even time, the main practical figure, is a counterfactual that was never simulated, and it shows no net force-time benefit for holds under about 16.6 s. Methodologically the work applies published CRC, LTT and quantile tracking with no new theory. Readability also suffers: the abstract and most paragraphs carry so many hedges and four-digit numbers that the main message is hard to follow.
strengths: Honest reporting throughout: the one confirmed pre-registered decision is clearly separated from secondary, post hoc and unadjusted rows; all 8 deviations from the pre-registration are listed; a sub-pool in which the method loses is reported prominently, including in the abstract.

Numbers are internally consistent across the abstract, Tables 1-4, Figure 1 and the text: matched-slip D 0.4563 can be recomputed from the Fig. 1b points; break-even and integrated force-time follow from the mean hold forces and the 17.96 / 31.04 N s phase integrals.

Sound calibration design: CRC on the monotonised physical binary loss gives a valid upper bound on physical slip, and the switch from the label route was motivated by a failed, pre-registered monotonicity gate.

The comparator is strong and was chosen beforehand: the friction-blind conformal baseline was picked on a disjoint selection split before any calibration or test access, against Mondrian (privileged family identity) and learned proprioceptive alternatives.

Careful attribution set: plug-in, shrunk plug-in, onset-only learner, feature chain, oracle-side friction prior, uniform and tuned margins. The tuned-margin result (it equals CRC at n = 500) is reported frankly.

The scope of the guarantee is stated precisely: marginal, per stratum, in expectation, needs counterfactual replays. Re-split, per-stratum and friction-quintile miscoverage are shown rather than hidden.
The force cost of the fixed protocol (preload, squeeze, probe force-time and break-even) is accounted for in newtons and N s rather than only in relative excess.
weaknesses: The headline effect is close to a design artefact: friction is log-uniform on [0.3, 1.0] and independent of every non-tactile input, so any friction-blind rule must pay for the whole range. D falls to 0.1401 at sigma 0.4 (lower limit below the SESOI) and reverses for mu in [0.5, 0.8]. No correlated-friction pool or deployable vision/category prior is tested, so the result says little about realistic object sets.

The central attribution claim (the saving comes from the probe, not the learner; probe + plug-in + CRC suffices), repeated in the abstract, novelty paragraph, discussion and conclusion, rests only on post hoc, unadjusted, slip-unmatched rows on a refined grid adopted after the primary-grid floor was seen. The pre-registered H2b and TOST tests are both not confirmed, and no pre-specified fresh-object replication exists.

The break-even time of 16.56 s, the main practical cost-benefit figure, assumes that a no-probe CSF-1 grasp holds the same 7.606 N. That grasp was never simulated, although it would be cheap to run in the existing simulator.
Onset noise sigma, which sets the effect size (D 0.68 to 0.14), is assumed and not grounded in hardware or published detector-error data.

Deployability gap: the offline certificate needs counterfactual replays at every grid force, so it exists only in simulation. The deployable online tracker has only a long-run-average guarantee, its intervals are over orderings of largely shared instances, H3 is inconclusive in all shifts, and the physical-replay oracle was not produced.

Methodological novelty is limited: CRC, LTT and score-space quantile tracking are applied as published, and reading friction from incipient slip is established. The contribution is an evaluation protocol plus a negative or attribution result.

Prior controllers are not reproduced (Khamis, Dong, Boonstra, Niu); the only reactive arm is a self-described flawed negative control (raw, upward-biased mu-hat threshold). The paper therefore cannot say whether probe + CRC beats existing tactile grip regulation at equal slip.

The fixed 32.7 N preload and 1.5 F0 squeeze are 10x the median minimal force and dominate force-time, which undercuts the 'minimal force' motivation (fragile or prosthetic handling) that the introduction invokes.

Readability: the abstract packs Holm values over two families, two grid routes, CI levels and four-digit numbers into one paragraph. The same hedges (post hoc, unadjusted, not slip-matched, grid floor) are repeated nearly verbatim in about 8 places, and the tables mix decision, route and grid information densely. The core message is hard to extract.

Too many inferential layers (four Bonferroni-split core decisions, Holm on 52 first-round secondaries, unadjusted second and third rounds, a downgrade-only refined-grid rule, test-selected matched slip). The decision status of any given number is hard to track, and several inferiority bounds sit within 0.02 of zero.
required_actions: [evidence-level] Run a pre-specified confirmatory replication of the attribution claim: fresh test objects, a pre-registered wide per-stratum grid with no floor for any arm, and slip-matched contrasts of learned vs (shrunk) plug-in and plug-in vs CSF-1. Otherwise demote 'the saving is in the probe / plug-in suffices' from the abstract, novelty paragraph and conclusion to an explicitly exploratory observation.

[evidence-level] Test the dependence on the design: add a pool in which friction is correlated with family or material and give the baseline a deployable non-tactile prior, plus a pre-specified friction-width sweep. This shows whether D survives outside the weak-by-construction setting, and also tests the 'narrow spread relative to probe error' reading of the mid-friction reversal.

[evidence-level] Simulate the no-probe CSF-1 grasp (same preload, no squeeze or probe phases, CRC-calibrated) so that the break-even time and the net force-time benefit are measured rather than assumed.

[evidence-level] Ground sigma: either use published incipient-slip detector error or a small hardware measurement, or report results over a sigma band presented as the primary result rather than a single assumed point.

[paper-level] Rewrite the abstract and the contributions for readability: one sentence for the confirmed result and its conditions, one for the conditionality (sigma, friction range, sign flip), one for the exploratory attribution. Move Holm and grid-route details to the body.

[paper-level] State the hedges once (e.g., a 'status of evidence' box or one table column) and refer to it, instead of repeating 'post hoc, unadjusted, not slip-matched, refined grid' in every section. Add a decision-status legend that applies across all tables.

[paper-level] Reframe the motivation and the title around what is actually shown (calibrated hold-force selection after a high-force probe protocol, in simulation). Either drop or temper the fragile-object and prosthetic framing in the introduction, given the 32.7 N preload and squeeze.
[paper-level] Remove the Figure 1 generation prompt from the manuscript body, keep only the caption, and supply an actual Figure 2 plot.
